claim: Cognyte did not appear from nowhere. Verint Systems "completed the spin-off of Cognyte Software Ltd." in 2021, with Cognyte trading on Nasdaq from February 2, 2021 — and Verint is the former Comverse Infosys, an Israeli-founded company that went public in 2002 selling lawful-interception ("wiretapping") software. Its STAR-GATE and RELIANT systems were installed inside telecom and internet carriers to intercept communications, on legal authorization, for law-enforcement and government agencies. The same corporate line was the subject of a contested December 2001 Fox News series by correspondent Carl Cameron, alleging Israeli-linked surveillance of US federal agencies including the DEA before 9/11; the reports were hedged as "inconclusive" and disputed at the time. That lineage — Comverse Infosys to Verint to Cognyte — now sells cell-site-simulator surveillance vans to American police.
